title: Review gates
lede: How a diff gets reviewed, fixed and verified before merge: two independent reviewers, one fixer, and a receipt so the same code is not checked twice.

gather.name: Gather the diff
gather.role: Collect the branch's diff and the full text of every changed file.
details: The diff is git diff main...HEAD.
For the whole repo instead of a diff, /audit ranks the worst files first.

reviewers.name: Two reviewers
reviewers.role: A correctness reviewer and a structure reviewer read the diff in parallel, without editing.

more: A test weakened to pass counts as a defect.
Scores the rubric and lists cleanups.
Checks diff economy and repeated code across files.

details: Each reviewer starts fresh, with no session context.
qs: Why run two separate reviewers instead of one?

merge.name: Merge findings
merge.role: Combine both reports into one ordered work list, correctness first.
details: Findings on the same lines become one item.
If both reviews are clean, the fix step is skipped.
Run standalone without --fix, it presents the list and waits for approval.

fixer.name: One fixer
fixer.role: A single agent applies the whole list, then re-runs the tests.
details: Only one agent edits, so two agents never change the same files at once.
risks: If a fix needs a test changed, it is surfaced, never weakened to pass.

reverify.name: Re-verify
reverify.role: A fresh check confirms correctness is clear and every rubric score is 10/10.
details: On a regression it fixes once more; if that still fails, it surfaces what remains and stops.

receipt.name: Receipt
receipt.role: A verified run writes a receipt for the exact code, so the merge step can reuse it.

more: A missing, mismatched or corrupt receipt means the checks re-run in full.

details: Full suites run only for shared core; other changes run the checks for the parts they touch.

deep.h: What the receipt is keyed to

qs: What counts as shared core, and why does it get the full suite?

rubric.d: Four scores for code: Quality, Readability, Encapsulation, Clarity.

economy.d: Added lines must earn their place; deletions count as credit.

shared.d: Public API, save formats, networking and workspace build inputs.

failclosed.d: When in doubt, block and re-run instead of passing.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold reviews, fixes and verifies a code change before it merges.
